title: Machine-learning feature selection yields a 239-gene urinary signature of early sepsis
summary: In a prospective cohort of 266 sepsis patients and 82 controls, urinary-cell RNA was profiled within 12 hours of sepsis onset, and multiple machine-learning ensembles selected a set of 239 genes that classified septic patients from those with chronic systemic disease in internal and independent external validation cohorts. Functional analysis indicated disrupted pathways in early sepsis. The abstract gives no AUC values, and the authors state that confirmation is still needed.
ai_technology: Machine-learning ensemble feature selection on urinary-cell gene expression
organization: University of Florida Health; University of Florida

evidence.tested: Internal and independent external validation cohorts for the 239-gene classifier.
evidence.unknown: Classification metrics and whether the signature complements blood-based tests; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning ensembles selected the discriminating gene subset.
